metadata.title: Claude, Customer Escalation.
metadata.purpose: Answer whether asking Claude to escalate a customer issue means it just forwards the complaint to whoever seems right, or something else, using the skill's real checklist (understand, gather context, assess impact, pick a tier, structure repro steps, generate the brief) with the skill's own documented Acme-500-errors example as the concrete case. Lands the carry-out that nothing is sent until the brief is built and confirmed.
metadata.anchor_pair: B01 -> B03 (the skill's own documented Acme-500-errors example, planted with the checklist; paid off showing the brief land on the Engineering tier and the confirm-before-send gate, plus the Handle-in-Support flip)

beats.narration_text: Someone tells Claude to escalate a customer bug, expecting it to just forward the complaint along. It doesn't — first it builds the case. So what actually happens before anything reaches engineering?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'Escalate this bug to engineering — just forward it, right?', hesitates on 'forward', corrects to 'package', lands the real question

beats.act: 1 stakes / 2 wrong guess, falsified / 4 ANCHOR PLANTED
beats.narration_text: Take a real example from the skill itself: API returning 500 errors intermittently for Acme Corp. Claude doesn't send that anywhere yet. It runs a fixed checklist first — what's broken, who's affected, how long it's been going on, what's already been tried — and checks that against its own rules for when an issue actually needs to escalate at all.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — the Acme-500-errors line types in over a checklist of four questions, each ticking off one at a time; nothing points anywhere yet

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — checklist first, no target yet
production_viz.mechanic: A short line types itself out at the top: "API returning 500 errors intermittently — Acme Corp." THE ANCHOR. Beneath it, four questions draw in one at a time, each getting a teal check as it lands: "What's broken?" / "Who's affected?" / "How long?" / "What's been tried?" No arrow, no destination card, no team name anywhere in frame. A caption beneath reads 'nothing sent yet.' THIS EXACT ANCHOR LINE RETURNS AT B03.

beats.narration_text: Only then does it decide who the case goes to — and that follows a fixed ladder, not a guess. Support escalations move up to senior support. Confirmed bugs go to engineering. Feature gaps go to product. Anything touching data exposure or access skips the ladder entirely and goes straight to security. And high-revenue churn risk, or a breached SLA on a critical account, goes to leadership.

shot.new_visual_element: A five-rung ladder card (Support / Engineering / Product / Security / Leadership); a marker climbs the first three rungs in order, then a separate line jumps straight to Security, then another reaches Leadership from outside the ladder

production_viz.label: A fixed ladder, not a guess
production_viz.mechanic: A vertical ladder card draws in with five rungs, bottom to top: Support, Engineering, Product, Security, Leadership. A small teal marker climbs from Support to Engineering, then to Product, one rung at a time, pausing on each. Then a separate terracotta line draws in from off-card straight to the Security rung, skipping the ladder — labelled 'bypasses the ladder.' A third line, also from off-card, reaches the Leadership rung directly. Caption beneath: 'the target follows the rules, not a guess.'

beats.narration_text: Back to Acme: the brief gets built — severity, impact, exact reproduction steps — and it lands with engineering, the right tier for a confirmed bug. But even then, Claude doesn't post it or message the customer on its own — it asks first. And the same checklist can go the other way: if the fix is already documented, the issue never escalates at all — it stays in support.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — the Acme checklist from B01, now all four checks lit, feeding a brief card that lands on the Engineering rung; a dashed 'waiting on your yes' box sits over it; a second branch shows the same checklist landing on 'documented fix' and stopping in a support lane, no brief at all

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — brief built, then it asks
production_viz.mechanic: THE B01 ANCHOR LINE RETURNS, identical: "API returning 500 errors intermittently — Acme Corp." All four checklist marks are already lit. A brief card slides in beneath it — labelled Severity / Impact / Repro steps — and a line connects it to the Engineering rung from B02. A dashed teal box wraps the whole thing with the caption 'waiting on your yes' — no send icon, no post icon anywhere. Below, a second, smaller branch draws in: the same four checks, but this time landing on a card reading 'documented fix' inside a flat grey 'support' lane — no brief card appears on this branch at all. Caption beneath: 'or it never escalates.'

beats.narration_text: Ask Claude to escalate a customer issue, and it doesn't forward anything — it builds the full case, picks the target by fixed tier rules, and waits for you to say go.

props.quote: Ask Claude to escalate a customer issue, and it doesn't forward anything — it builds the full case, picks the target by fixed tier rules, and waits for you to say go.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Describe a real support issue to Claude — a bug, a slow response, an angry customer — and ask it to run the customer-escalation checklist before doing anything else. Then watch: does it build a full brief and ask before sending or posting it, or does it just react? Liam, in for Bear.

props.command: I have a customer issue: [describe it]. Read the customer-escalation skill and walk me through what you'd check before deciding whether to escalate — and don't send or post anything until I say go.
